learningObjectives: Differentiate Pega GenAI tools and their intended uses
Generate and review a Case Type, Life Cycle and Data Model with Autopilot
Generate and review Personas with Autopilot
Generate sample data records and populate testing forms with Autopilot

elements.description: A suite of generative AI-powered features integrated across Pega Platform, available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. It helps developers, learners, and users build applications, enhance learning, improve operational efficiency, and stay aligned with best practices.

elements.text: Autopilot is a drafting assistant: use the proposal as a starting point, then check it against requirements. It does not know every implementation or replace professional validation.

elements.description: A separate SaaS design tool for collaborative application proposals. Review its suggested Case Types, data and Personas, then import the Blueprint into Pega Platform to accelerate development. The proposal is not automatically a production-ready application or a delivery-time guarantee.

Design-time AI features in App Studio assist with workflow, fields, Personas and testing data. Review recommendations in context; claims about development-speed improvements are not a measured guarantee for an individual project.
Lets you develop custom Pega GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway; an add-on compatible with Pega Platform, Customer Service, or Sales Automation.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: GenAI Run-Time Tools and Custom AI

elements.description: Provides expert advice and feedback on END-USER tasks at application RUNTIME — ideal for task-specific guidance relevant to a Pega Case.

elements.term: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
elements.description: Automate Case processing and provide conversational support for run-time users. Agents perform automated actions and offer run-time guidance to accelerate Case processing; Tool Rules add governance, security, and compliance.

Conversational answers grounded in an organization’s procedural documents and knowledge bases, useful while learning, developing or working. It can provide client-specific context; it is not restricted to generic employee questions.

Search Assistant integrates with Pega Community search (powered by Knowledge Buddy) to link relevant materials. OpenAI search on the Pega Documentation site answers questions when you add a question mark to the end of a search query.

elements.term: Blueprint as a SaaS design tool
elements.description: Blueprint rapidly and collaboratively designs new applications and Case Types and operates INDEPENDENTLY as a SaaS tool — no Pega instance required to collaborate. The result imports into Pega Platform to jumpstart development.

From a business-terms description, Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, plus best-practice application templates, enabling quick design edits to fit requirements.

Since Pega Infinity '24, configure a Connect Generative AI Step in App Studio. A Connect Rule begins with a Prompt — the request for information sent to the Pega GenAI engine, custom to the Step or reused from Dev Studio.
GenAI response types and their Data Model mapping:
items: Structured - Single: one page/paragraph or field+value, auto-mapped to a Data Model field
Structured - List: bulleted fields/values mapped to an embedded data list
Unstructured: long/complex output — best practice is to map to a Text (paragraph) field

elements.description: You must identify a target field to write the response into, and add that target field to the application UI so the response can be displayed to the user.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules

elements.description: Configurable AI assistants that automate Case processing and offer run-time guidance. An agent can run an automation, start a Case, call another agent, or launch a user action. Extend reach via agent-to-agent or MCP protocols.

Detailed descriptions and guardrails ensure the agent responds precisely; at run time users converse with agents in natural-language chat. Agents can also process and extract data from uploaded documents, saving manual analysis time.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generating a Case Type and Data Model

elements.description: In App Studio’s Case Type tab, choose a suggested name or enter your own. Suggestions use the application name and metadata. Select the Autopilot option to propose a Life Cycle and Data Model.

Check and modify Stages and Steps against stakeholder requirements. Next proposes fields with Name, Type and technical ID. Edit names/types, add fields or remove unsuitable suggestions. Embedded Data and Data reference proposals can create associated data objects.
Submit after review. Inspect the created Life Cycle on Workflow and the fields on Data model. A generated proposal is not proof that workflow, integration or security requirements are satisfied.

Select a data object and open Records. Generate sample records with Autopilot and specify the desired number. The generated values correspond to field types; they can support tests before external data integration is available.
While testing a Case, Fill form with AI populates its form fields. These values become part of the Case data used during processing; they are test samples rather than verified production records.

Open Users > User management in App Studio. Autopilot proposes Persona names and descriptions from application metadata. Choose a proposal or enter a custom name, then review it against real stakeholder responsibilities.
After creation, add the Persona through the Case Life Cycle’s Personas & Channels area. Generating the business user model is not a guarantee of complete authorization or routing configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Design-time vs. run-time tools
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam tests whether a tool acts at design time or run time. Blueprint and Autopilot are DESIGN-time; Coach and Agents are RUN-time.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map each tool to its phase: Blueprint/Autopilot = build the app; Coach/Agents = help users while the app runs.

examPitfalls.title: Release-specific Autopilot defaults
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic states Autopilot features are inactive by default in Infinity 23 and 24. Availability and enablement depend on the target release and configuration; do not turn this historical note into an all-version rule.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify the relevant feature and environment configuration instead of assuming availability means activation.

examPitfalls.title: Always review AI suggestions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks the recommended action after Autopilot or Blueprint generates content. Candidates say 'accept and publish immediately.' GenAI suggestions must always be reviewed by a human before publishing — auto-acceptance is not recommended practice.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Human-in-the-loop: review and modify recommendations (Case Types, fields, Personas, data) before generating.

examPitfalls.title: Coach vs. Knowledge Buddy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Coach gives task-specific advice on a Case at run time; Knowledge Buddy answers questions from the org's procedural docs/knowledge bases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Task advice on a specific Case → Coach. Conversational answers from knowledge bases → Knowledge Buddy.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint independence and import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Blueprint collaboration is independent of a Pega Platform instance/Operator login. This does not claim that the SaaS has no sign-in or collaboration-access requirements. PremBridge is not required for Blueprint import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember: Blueprint augments (not replaces) App Studio; import needs no PremBridge.

examPitfalls.title: Connect Step response structures
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Connect Generative AI is not the same as a Connect REST response-mapping exercise. The topic distinguishes Structured-Single, Structured-List and Unstructured responses and requires a response target.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Single → field/short page; List → embedded data list; Unstructured/long/JSON → Text (paragraph) field. Always set a target field and add it to the UI.

examPitfalls.title: What Autopilot can generate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Autopilot generates Case Types (with Life Cycle and Data Model), Personas, sample data records, form fill, and Insights — not production integrations or security.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tie Autopilot to design-time generation of workflow, data, Personas, and sample data.

examPitfalls.title: Agent capabilities
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Agents can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, launch user actions, and extract data from uploaded documents — governed by Tool Rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember: a Pega Agent combines conversation and action capabilities; Tool Rules define what the Agent is authorized to do, serving as its governance guardrails.

practiceQuiz.scenario: While building a new 'Claims Processing' application in App Studio, a developer wants real-time, context-aware suggestions for Case Types, Data Model fields, and Personas as they configure. Which Pega GenAI capability provides this?

options.text: Pega GenAI Autopilot — the design-time AI assistant embedded in App Studio that generates Case Types, fields, and Personas from context
Pega GenAI Coach — provides expert, context-aware suggestions to the developer during the App Studio build process
Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy — surfaces recommendations from Pega documentation and knowledge bases during App Studio sessions
Pega GenAI Search Assistant — the AI-powered docs.pega.com search that surfaces relevant documentation while the developer builds

practiceQuiz.hint: Design-time suggestions inside App Studio for Case Types, fields, and Personas.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega GenAI Autopilot is the design-time AI assistant embedded in App Studio — it generates Case Types, fields, and Personas as the SA builds. Coach is a runtime tool for end users, not a design-time assistant for developers.

optionExplanations.A: Autopilot supports the stated design-time application authoring task.
optionExplanations.B: Coach guides runtime case work rather than this modeling task.
optionExplanations.C: Knowledge retrieval is different from generating these application components.
optionExplanations.D: Documentation search does not generate the requested application configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Claims Service Representative is handling a complex customer complaint in Pega. They need expert, step-by-step guidance on how to resolve the current Case. Which GenAI tool is designed to help them at runtime?

options.text: Pega GenAI Coach — delivers expert, task-specific runtime guidance to end users working on their current Case
Pega GenAI Autopilot — assists the user by generating the next best Case step automatically in real time
Pega Blueprint — the SaaS design tool that produces a guided resolution template from the complaint description
OpenAI Search — the AI-powered search embedded in Pega that retrieves resolution guidance from Pega's documentation

practiceQuiz.hint: Runtime advice for an end user working a live Case — which GenAI tool is this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Coach is intended for task-specific guidance during Case work. Autopilot supports authoring and testing, including filling running test forms; saying it has no role after deployment is too broad.

optionExplanations.A: Coach fits context-specific guidance while a user works a case.
optionExplanations.B: Design-time generation does not answer the user's runtime guidance need.
optionExplanations.C: Blueprint proposes an application design rather than coaching this case worker.
optionExplanations.D: Documentation search is not task-specific runtime case coaching.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A project manager asks which Pega GenAI tools operate at DESIGN time to help build the application before any users interact with it. Which TWO are correct?

options.text: Pega Blueprint — a standalone SaaS tool that uses natural language to generate an initial application design (Case Types, Data Models, Personas) before any development begins
Pega GenAI Autopilot — embedded in App Studio, provides real-time design-time suggestions for Case Types, fields, and workflows as the SA configures
Pega GenAI Coach — operates at design time, generating coaching content for end users before the application goes live
Pega GenAI Agent — a runtime automation capability that handles end-user requests and executes actions within a live application

practiceQuiz.hint: Design-time = used while building the app; runtime = used while working Cases.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes application designs and Autopilot assists configuration in App Studio. Coach and Agents address application work rather than the design task asked here.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint supports collaborative initial application design.
optionExplanations.B: App Studio suggestions require the authoring context, unlike the proposed SaaS design.
optionExplanations.C: Coach is not the initial application proposal tool.
optionExplanations.D: Runtime agents orchestrate actions rather than this pre-build design task.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A senior SA asks a junior: 'Why haven't we seen any Autopilot suggestions since we upgraded to Pega Infinity '24 three months ago? No one has mentioned needing to activate it.' The junior responds: 'I thought Autopilot was on by default in Infinity '24 because the release notes mentioned GenAI features.' Which statement best identifies the gap and the fix?

options.text: Autopilot features are INACTIVE by default in Pega Infinity '23 and '24 and must be explicitly configured and enabled — the release notes describe availability, not default enablement
Autopilot only activates in Dev Studio, not in App Studio — since the team works in App Studio, they will never see Autopilot suggestions without switching studios
Autopilot was available in Infinity '23 but was removed in Infinity '24 due to compliance concerns; the team must downgrade to '23 to regain it
Autopilot requires the PremBridge license add-on, which is separate from the base Pega Infinity license — the team must contact their account manager

practiceQuiz.hint: Is a feature being 'available' the same as being 'on by default'?
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Autopilot is available but INACTIVE by default and requires explicit configuration and enablement. Release notes announce availability, not default activation.

optionExplanations.A: Availability in these releases still requires enabling the configured features.
optionExplanations.B: The suggestions are not restricted to Dev Studio.
optionExplanations.C: The cited release did not remove the available features.
optionExplanations.D: The described enablement gap does not establish a required PremBridge license.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Autopilot recommends a 5-Stage Claims workflow and 12 picklist values for a 'Claim Type' field. The developer is tempted to accept all recommendations immediately. What does Pega's guidance say?

options.text: Review and modify the recommendations before generating — Pega explicitly states it is not responsible for AI-generated content, and human oversight is required
Accept all recommendations automatically — Autopilot's suggestions are guaranteed accurate because they are generated from the application's own data model
Submit them to the LSA for Java compilation before generating — AI-generated rules require manual compilation before they can run
Export them to Blueprint first so Blueprint can validate the recommendations against best-practice templates before generating

practiceQuiz.hint: Who is responsible for the accuracy of AI-generated content in Pega?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega explicitly states it is not responsible for the content of AI-generated suggestions — the developer must review and validate every recommendation before accepting it. AI-generated outputs are proposals, not approved configurations.

optionExplanations.A: Review generated suggestions against the actual business requirements.
optionExplanations.B: Generated content is not guaranteed correct merely because it uses context.
optionExplanations.C: Manual Java compilation is not the review step requested.
optionExplanations.D: Exporting to another design tool is not a required review gate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business analyst describes a new 'Commercial Insurance' application to Pega Blueprint in plain business language. Which THREE items can Blueprint propose from this description?

options.text: Case Types and Case Life Cycles
Data Models and data objects
Personas
Production server hardware and network topology

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint proposes the application design skeleton — what does a Pega application skeleton contain?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes the application design: Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas — the full skeleton of a Pega application. D is wrong because Blueprint is a design tool for Pega application structure, not an infrastructure planning tool; it does not design servers, networks, or hardware.

optionExplanations.A: A proposed workflow can include case models and their lifecycles.
optionExplanations.B: The proposal can describe the business data model.
optionExplanations.C: The design can include the intended user groups.
optionExplanations.D: Application design proposals do not provision server and network infrastructure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business stakeholder wants to join a Blueprint session to co-design the application with the SA. The stakeholder does not have a Pega Platform login. Can they participate?

options.text: Yes — Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool that requires no Pega Platform instance or login for collaboration; the stakeholder can participate directly
No — Blueprint requires every participant to have an active Pega Platform login; the stakeholder must be created as an Operator first
Yes — but the stakeholder can only view, not contribute; only users with an LSA license can modify a Blueprint session
No — Blueprint is embedded inside Dev Studio and is inaccessible without Dev Studio credentials and the correct Ruleset access

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool — does it require a Pega Platform login?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint is a standalone SaaS application — no Pega Platform instance or login is required. Business stakeholders can collaborate on Blueprint without an Operator account.

optionExplanations.A: A Pega Platform Operator login is not required for this independent design tool.
optionExplanations.B: This wrongly requires a Platform identity for the SaaS design activity.
optionExplanations.C: The stated LSA-only editing restriction is not the collaboration model.
optionExplanations.D: Blueprint is not restricted to the Dev Studio interface.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Connect Generative AI Step returns a narrative claim summary as unstructured text — potentially several paragraphs long. Per Pega best practices, which Field Type should be the target for this response?

options.text: Text (paragraph) — the appropriate Field Type for long, unstructured text content such as AI-generated narratives
Currency — handles large numeric values that may be embedded in financial claim summaries from the AI response
Boolean — the AI response is ultimately a pass/fail decision, so Boolean is the most compact representation
Date only — the claim summary includes a date field, so Date only captures the most critical structured element

practiceQuiz.hint: Unstructured, potentially multi-paragraph narrative → which Field Type accommodates this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Text (paragraph) is the recommended target for long or complex unstructured responses. It retains narrative content rather than coercing it into Currency, Boolean or Date; the topic does not promise unlimited field size.

optionExplanations.A: Paragraph text fits a narrative response that must retain its content.
optionExplanations.B: A numeric currency field cannot preserve the narrative.
optionExplanations.C: A Boolean would discard the explanatory content.
optionExplanations.D: A date field would discard everything except a date value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA configures a Connect Generative AI Step and needs to choose how the response will be structured. Which TWO are valid response structure types for a GenAI Connect Step?

options.text: Structured - Single — maps a single field/value pair (or short page) from the AI response to a Data Model field
Structured - List — maps a list of field/value pairs from the AI response to an embedded data list
Encrypted - Binary — maps binary output (image or file) from the AI to a Pega Attachment rule
Compiled - Java — maps the AI response to a Java-compiled rule for processing in the Dev Studio Rules layer

practiceQuiz.hint: The three valid structures are Structured-Single, Structured-List, and Unstructured — which two appear here?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Structured-Single and Structured-List are two documented response structures. Unstructured is the third. Encrypted-Binary and Compiled-Java are not the listed structures.

optionExplanations.A: A single structured response can map into the target data model.
optionExplanations.B: A structured list response can map into an embedded list.
optionExplanations.C: This is not one of the listed response structures.
optionExplanations.D: Compiled Java is not a response structure for this automation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA configures a Connect Generative AI Step that maps the response to a 'ClaimSummary' Text (paragraph) field. The SA runs a test but cannot see the summary on the Case form. What additional step is required?

options.text: Add the 'ClaimSummary' field to the Case View (form) so the response is displayed to the user
Lock the Ruleset containing the Connect Step — unlocked Rulesets do not render AI responses in the UI
Create an Access Role granting 'read' permission to the 'ClaimSummary' field for the user's Persona
Enable Unattended RPA on the Connect Step — AI-generated content requires robotic processing before it can be displayed

practiceQuiz.hint: A target field was mapped — but where must the field appear for the user to see it?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Mapping the GenAI response to ClaimSummary writes data to the clipboard, but users cannot see it until the field is added to the Case View (the form UI). Clipboard storage and UI display are two separate steps.

optionExplanations.A: Display the response target in a View so the user can see it.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset locking is not a condition for rendering the response field.
optionExplanations.C: An invented field-read permission step does not place the field in the UI.
optionExplanations.D: RPA is not required to display a generated narrative.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An HR employee needs instant answers about the company's leave policies, benefits procedures, and onboarding checklist — all documented in internal knowledge bases. Which Pega GenAI tool is designed for this?

options.text: Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy — combines GenAI with organization-specific knowledge bases to answer employee questions conversationally
Pega GenAI Coach — provides expert task-specific guidance to employees on their current open Cases
Pega GenAI Autopilot — surfaces relevant policy recommendations from the employee's App Studio design context
Pega Blueprint — generates a proposed leave-policy workflow from the employee's natural-language question

practiceQuiz.hint: Organization-specific knowledge bases + conversational Q&A for employees = which tool?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Knowledge Buddy uses organizational knowledge sources for conversational answers. Its contextual information can help learning, development and work; this is not an exclusion of customer-facing uses.

optionExplanations.A: Knowledge Buddy can answer using the organization's knowledge sources.
optionExplanations.B: Coach is oriented toward guidance for the user's case task.
optionExplanations.C: Application authoring suggestions do not answer this employee knowledge question.
optionExplanations.D: Designing a workflow is different from retrieving policy knowledge.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring Pega GenAI Agents with Tool Rules. A stakeholder asks what these agents can do. Which TWO capabilities are enabled?

options.text: Run an automation, start a Case, call another agent, or launch a user action — agents can orchestrate Pega capabilities as tools
Process and extract structured data from uploaded documents during a conversation with the user
Replace security and compliance controls — agents can self-authorize actions without requiring Access Roles or Operator permissions
Compile the application's Ruleset — agents can generate and deploy Java-compiled rules without developer intervention

practiceQuiz.hint: Orchestration of Pega capabilities + document processing — two things GenAI Agents with Tool Rules can do.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Agents can use configured tools to orchestrate case actions and process uploaded documents. Agent actions remain subject to the application security model and guardrails; they do not self-authorize.

optionExplanations.A: Configured tools can orchestrate supported application actions.
optionExplanations.B: Agents can process uploaded documents during conversation.
optionExplanations.C: Agents do not replace authorization or authorize themselves.
optionExplanations.D: Rule compilation and deployment are not unconstrained agent powers.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to this module’s cited documentation-search guidance, how does a learner request an AI answer on the Pega Documentation site?

options.text: Append a question mark to the search query — 'Connect Generative AI Step response types?' — which triggers the OpenAI-powered search mode on the docs site
Prefix the query with 'AI:' to switch the docs site into AI-answer mode — 'AI: Connect Generative AI Step response types'
Enable PremBridge in their developer portal settings first, which unlocks AI-powered search as a premium feature on the docs site
Open Prediction Studio and use the integrated documentation search there, which provides AI-synthesized answers unlike the main docs.pega.com site

practiceQuiz.hint: On docs.pega.com, the AI mode is triggered by a specific character at the END of the query.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cited curriculum describes ending the search question with a question mark. This is versioned learning guidance, not a claim that no other search interaction or newer interface exists.

optionExplanations.A: The cited documentation-search guidance uses a question-mark query.
optionExplanations.B: This invented prefix is not the documented trigger in the curriculum.
optionExplanations.C: PremBridge settings are not the search-mode prerequisite described.
optionExplanations.D: The question asks about the documentation site, not model authoring.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants to develop a custom AI-assisted contract-summary capability through the Pega GenAI gateway. Which tool provides the custom-capability extension point?

options.text: Pega GenAI Connect — an add-on that lets developers build custom GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway
Pega GenAI Coach — can be customized to perform contract analysis by training it on the organization's contract library
Pega GenAI Search Assistant — the AI-powered docs.pega.com search can be extended with custom knowledge sources like contract libraries
Pega Blueprint — generates a contract-analysis workflow from a natural-language description of the analysis requirements

practiceQuiz.hint: Custom GenAI capability + Pega GenAI gateway add-on = which tool?
practiceQuiz.rationale: GenAI Connect supports custom capabilities through the GenAI gateway. This identifies the extension point; it does not guarantee that every arbitrary model is supported without configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Connect provides the extension point for custom GenAI functionality.
optionExplanations.B: Case coaching is not the custom integration mechanism requested.
optionExplanations.C: Documentation search is not the organization's contract-analysis integration.
optionExplanations.D: A proposed workflow does not implement the custom AI capability by itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The curriculum identifies the introduction of the Pega GenAI suite beginning with which Pega Infinity release? Distinguish this milestone from availability requirements for individual tools.

options.text: Pega Infinity '23 — individual features have their own release, configuration and service requirements
GenAI features were introduced in Pega Infinity '21 — a client on '22 already has full access and may simply need to enable the features in their configuration
GenAI features require Pega Platform 8.6 or higher; they are version-independent and available in all Infinity releases including '22 through a license flag
Only Pega Blueprint is available from Pega Infinity '22; Autopilot, Coach, and Knowledge Buddy require upgrading to '24 or later

practiceQuiz.hint: When was the Pega GenAI suite first introduced — and is '22 before or after that release?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The curriculum identifies Infinity '23 as the suite-introduction milestone. It does not establish that every named tool shipped in that release, or that standalone Blueprint collaboration requires a Platform upgrade.

optionExplanations.A: The curriculum dates the suite introduction, not every individual feature.
optionExplanations.B: This claims full availability in an earlier release without support.
optionExplanations.C: A license flag does not make all features independent of release support.
optionExplanations.D: This is not the curriculum's stated suite-introduction milestone.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer wants to test the Claims Processing form with realistic data without manually typing values into every field. Which Autopilot capabilities help?

options.text: Generate sample records for a data object and auto-fill a running Case's form fields with realistic sample data
Provision a production-grade database pre-populated with historical claim records for immediate testing
Mark existing rules as relevant record types so the platform auto-selects them as test data sources
Lock the topmost Ruleset version so the sample data cannot overwrite production records

practiceQuiz.hint: Sample data generation + form auto-fill for testing = two Autopilot capabilities.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Autopilot can generate sample records for a data object and automatically fill a running Case's form with realistic test values — making test setup significantly faster than manual data entry.

optionExplanations.A: Sample records and form values support the described development testing.
optionExplanations.B: Generated samples do not provision a production historical database.
optionExplanations.C: Relevant-record flags do not generate the requested example values.
optionExplanations.D: Locking a ruleset is not the sample-data generation mechanism.

quickRecap.value: Suite of generative AI features across Pega Platform since Pega Infinity '23.
Blueprint (SaaS pre-build design) and Autopilot (App Studio acceleration: Case Types, Data Model, Personas, sample data, Insights).
Coach (end-user task advice on a Case) and Agent/Tool Rules (automate Case processing + conversational support with guardrails).

Knowledge Buddy answers from organizational knowledge sources during learning, development or work. Search Assistant helps Community search; the cited docs-search guidance describes question-mark queries.
Inactive by default in '23/'24; always review/modify suggestions (Pega not responsible for content).
Separate SaaS collaboration without a Pega Platform instance/Operator login; review the design and import it. PremBridge is not required for Blueprint import.
Define a Prompt; responses: Structured-Single, Structured-List, Unstructured (→ Text paragraph). Set a target field and add it to the UI; can mask data + localize.
Run automations, start Cases, call agents, launch user actions, extract document data; Tool Rules provide governance/security.
